headword: {超高層|ちょうこうそう}ビル

definitions.explanation: An extremely tall building, typically over 100 meters or roughly 20 stories or more. The term specifically refers to buildings that tower above the surrounding cityscape.

examples.japanese: {新宿|しんじゅく}には{超高層|ちょうこうそう}ビルが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many skyscrapers in Shinjuku.

examples.japanese: あの{超高層|ちょうこうそう}ビルは{地上|ちじょう}60{階建|かいだ}てだ。
{駅前|えきまえ}に{新|あたら}しい{超高層|ちょうこうそう}ビルが{建設|けんせつ}{中|ちゅう}で、{完成|かんせい}すればこの{地域|ちいき}で{最|もっと}も{高|たか}い{建物|たてもの}になる。
examples.english: A new skyscraper is under construction in front of the station, and once completed it will be the tallest building in this area.

notes:
A compound of {超|ちょう} (super, ultra), {高層|こうそう} (high-rise), and ビル (building). In Japan, buildings over about 60 meters (roughly 20 stories) are generally classified as {超高層|ちょうこうそう}. Japan's tallest building is {麻布台|あざぶだい}ヒルズ{森|もり}JPタワー at 330 meters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {超高層|ちょうこうそう}ビルが{建|た}つ: a skyscraper is built
- {超高層|ちょうこうそう}ビル{群|ぐん}: a cluster of skyscrapers
- {超高層|ちょうこうそう}マンション: super high-rise apartment building
- {超高層|ちょうこうそう}ビルの{展望台|てんぼうだい}: observation deck of a skyscraper

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {高層|こうそう}ビル: high-rise building — tall but not as extreme as {超高層|ちょうこうそう}
- タワー: tower — often used for landmark towers and communication towers
- ビル: building — the general term for any multi-story building
